{{Short description|German theoretical physicist (born 1974)}}
{{BLP sources|date=February 2026}}

'''Harald Pfeiffer''' (born 1974) is a German astrophysicist at the [[University of Potsdam]].

== Education and career ==
Pfeiffer attended the Steigerwald-Landschulheim-Weisentheid, graduating in 1993. In 1993, he participated in the [[International Physics Olympiad]], winning a gold medal. He studied physics at the [[University of Bayreuth]] from 1994 to 1997, before continuing to the [[University of Cambridge]] from 1997 to 1998. Following this, he attended [[Cornell University]], completing his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 2003. Between 2003 and 2009, he was employed at [[California Institute of Technology]], first as a Sherman Fairchild Postdoctoral Scholar, and then as a Senior Postdoctoral Scholar. He then took up a position as associate, and then assistant, professor at the [[Canadian Institute for Theoretical Astrophysics]], [[University of Toronto]].<ref name = "HaraldPfeiffer">{{cite web |title=Prof.Harald Pfeiffer |url=https://www.aei.mpg.de/person/54205/2784 |website=Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics |access-date=7 February 2026}}</ref>

Since 2017, Pfeiffer has been a group leader in the Astrophysical and Cosmological Relativity department at the [[Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics]] in Potsdam, and a professor at the university of Potsdam.<ref name = "HaraldPfeiffer" />

== Research interests ==
Pfeiffer's work focuses on the applications of numerical relativity to gravitational wave astronomy. He develops methods to solve problems from gravitational physics using supercomputers. In particular, he uses simulations to answer questions about the emission of gravitational radiation from binary systems of [[Binary black hole|black holes]] or [[Neutron star merger|neutron stars]]. He is involved in the analysis of detector data from [[LIGO]], [[Virgo interferometer|Virgo]], and [[KAGRA]], and also works on the development of new experiments such as LISA.<ref>{{cite web |title=Harald Pfeiffer elected Fellow of the American Physical Society |url=https://www.aei.mpg.de/1084433/harald-pfeiffer-elected-fellow-of-the-american-physical-society |website=Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics |access-date=7 February 2026}}</ref>

Together with Lawrence Kidder and Mark School, he is a lead developer of the Spectral Einstein Code (SpEC), which solves numerically the partial differential equations describing compact binary coalescences. Using this code, they are able to predict the gravitational waveforms produced by such systems, which can then be searched for in detector data.<ref>{{cite web |title=SpEC: Spectral Einstein Code |url=https://www.black-holes.org/for-researchers/spec |website=Black-holes.org |publisher=SXS Collaboration |access-date=8 February 2026}}</ref>

Pfeiffer is also interested in improving the theoretical understanding of the properties of the [[Einstein Field Equations]], and exploring possible alternative theories of gravity.<ref name = "HaraldPfeiffer" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nee, Lara, Pfeiffer, Vu |title=Quasistationary hair for binary black hole initial data in scalar Gauss-Bonnet gravity |journal=Physical Review D |date=24 January 2025 |issue=111 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.111.024061|doi-access=free |arxiv=2406.08410 }}</ref>

== Awards ==

* 2015: [[Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel Research Award]]<ref name = "HumboldtStiftung">{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Harald P.Pfeiffer |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/vernetzen/recherche-im-humboldt-netzwerk/einzelansicht/1162148/prof-dr-harald-p-pfeiffer |website=Humboldt Foundation |publisher=Alexander von Humboldt Stiftung |access-date=7 February 2026}}</ref>
* 2016: Special Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics<ref name = "HumboldtStiftung" />
* 2016: Gruber Cosmology Prize<ref name = "HumboldtStiftung" />
* 2023: Fellow of the American Physical Society, for his leadership and numerous high-impact research contributions to the field of numerical relativity, which have greatly helped to interpret gravitational-wave observations of binary black holes.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Rubrik: Menschen |journal=Physik Journal |date=December 2023 |volume=22 |issue=12 |page=51 |ISSN=1617-9439 |url=https://pro-physik.de/zeitschriften/download/21840}}</ref>
